paper_sections.title: Patterns of Signal Change During Negative-Valence IAPS Image Presentation
Differences in PPI Between BWS and CON During HANS Presentation

description.value: The study compared hemodynamic brain responses and task-related functional connectivity during affective image presentation between big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers.

design.value: An event-related fMRI study comparing big wave surfers and non-big wave surfers while they viewed positive and negative, high- and low-arousal images from the International Affective Picture System.

description.value: Measured participants’ subjective emotional responses to the IAPS images.
Measured self-reported levels of sensation seeking across intensity of an experience and novelty of an experience scales.
Assessed participants’ positive and negative feelings experienced over the past week.
Assessed self-reported levels of fear toward various circumstances, objects, or other stimuli.
Those who regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

inclusion_criteria.value: Regularly surfed waves >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

exclusion_criteria.value: Experiencing claustrophobia upon entering the fMRI scanner; falling asleep during the fMRI scan.

recruitment_method.value: A convenience sample of 25 surfers were recruited for this study.

clinical_characteristics.value: Professional or semi-professional: 12; surfing experience: 26 ± 8 years; current surfing activity: 13 ± 10 hours/week.

description.value: Those who had not surfed waves of >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

inclusion_criteria.value: Had not surfed waves of >20 feet in height using the Hawaiian measurement system.

exclusion_criteria.value: Experiencing claustrophobia upon entering the fMRI scanner; falling asleep during the fMRI scan.

recruitment_method.value: A convenience sample of 25 surfers were recruited for this study.

clinical_characteristics.value: Professional or semi-professional: 1; surfing experience: 21 ± 10 years; current surfing activity: 6 ± 3 hours/week.

task_description.value: Participants viewed a series of images from the International Affective Picture System while undergoing brain fMRI. The task consisted of 180 trials lasting 7.5 min.

design_type.value: event-related design with jittered inter-stimulus interval

instructions.value: Participants were asked to view all images presented on the screen. No tasks related to regulation were instructed.

stimuli.value: 160 IAPS images: 40 each of high arousal positive, high arousal negative, low arousal positive, and low arousal negative; photographs were edited to reduce saturation by 30%.

task_performance_measures.value: After the fMRI, participants were asked whether they were able to remain attentive to all images.

instrument.value: 3 T MRI scanner (Achieva, Philips, Best, Netherlands)

description.value: Functional BOLD signals were acquired with a multi-shot gradient echo echoplanar imaging (EPI) sequence. Twenty-two axial slices covering the whole brain were acquired.

Images were realigned, slice-time corrected, mean-image constructed, co-registered with the high-resolution structural image, segmented and normalized using affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation, and smoothed with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: Construction of a mean functional image volume per subject per run
Co-registration with the high-resolution structural image
Affine registration followed by nonlinear transformation
Application of structural normalization parameters to functional image volumes
Spatial smoothing with an 8-mm Gaussian kernel at full width at half maximum

hrf_model.value: canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative

model_settings.value: Image onset in each trial was convolved with a canonical hemodynamic response function and its temporal derivative. Realignment parameters in all six dimensions were entered in the model. High-pass filtering used a 1/128 Hz cutoff, and serial autocorrelation was corrected by a first-degree autoregressive or AR(1) model.
Group: BWS vs. CON; arousal: high vs. low; valence: negative vs. positive.

HAP, HAN, LAP, LAN, and FIX formed the psychological regressors. The psychological regressors, physiological variable of the region of interest, and PPI variables were entered as regressors in a whole-brain GLM.

estimator.value: random-effect group analysis using positive contrast images

description.value: Positive-valence IAPS images with high arousal ratings.
Negative-valence IAPS images with high arousal ratings.
Positive-valence IAPS images with low arousal ratings.
Negative-valence IAPS images with low arousal ratings.
Trials in which no image was presented and participants continued to view a fixation cross.

definition.value: BWS > CON during HAN vs. FIX, with age as a covariate.

interpretations.value: The BWS group showed significantly increased activation in the visual cortex and insula compared with CON during HAN image presentation.

roi_definition.value: an a priori anatomical region defined using the WFU Pick Atlas

definition.value: CON > BWS during HAN vs. FIX, tested within the hypothalamus mask, with age as a covariate.

interpretations.value: The CON group showed significantly increased activity in the hypothalamus compared with the BWS group during HAN image presentation.

name.value: BWS > CON (LAN vs. FIX), periaqueductal gray

roi_definition.value: a separate functional/anatomical atlas mask from the Harvard Ascending Arousal Network (AAN) Atlas

definition.value: BWS > CON during LAN vs. FIX, tested within the periaqueductal gray mask, with age as a covariate.

interpretations.value: Significantly increased activation of the periaqueductal gray was observed in the BWS group compared with the CON group during LAN image presentation.

definition.value: BWS > CON during HAN vs. LAN, with age as a covariate.

interpretations.value: Significantly increased activation of the visual cortex was observed in the BWS group compared with the CON group during the HAN versus LAN comparison.

name.value: Insula PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

definition.value: CON > BWS in generalized PPI during HAN presentation, using the insula as the seed region, with age as a covariate.

target_regions.value: orbitofrontal, inferior frontal, superior temporal, and precentral cortices; prefrontal gyrus

parameter_change.value: CON group showed significantly increased incidence of PPIs

interpretations.value: Evidence of functional connectivity during HAN presentation was seen between the insula and the orbitofrontal, inferior frontal and superior temporal cortices, and the prefrontal gyrus in the CON group.

name.value: Hypothalamus PPI of HAN vs. FIX: CON > BWS

definition.value: CON > BWS in generalized PPI during HAN presentation, using the hypothalamus as the seed region, with age as a covariate.

target_regions.value: insula, superior temporal cortex, precentral gyrus, and middle frontal cortex

parameter_change.value: CON group showed significantly increased incidence of PPIs

interpretations.value: During HAN image presentation, the CON group showed significantly increased PPI between the hypothalamus and the insula, superior temporal cortex, precentral gyrus, and middle frontal cortex.
